title: Number of Ways to Assign Edge Weights I
summary: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered 1 to n, rooted at node 1, assign each edge a weight of 1 or 2.
statement: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered 1 to n, rooted at node 1, assign each edge a weight of 1 or 2. Choose a node x at the deepest level. Calculate the number of ways to assign weights to the path from node 1 to x so that the total cost is odd, modulo 10^9 + 7. Exclude edges not on this path.
constraints: edges form a tree of up to 100,000 nodes labeled 1 through n and rooted at 1.
Choose any deepest node and consider only its root path.
Assign each path edge weight one or two; count assignments with odd total modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: On a path of positive length d, toggling one chosen edge between weights one and two pairs every odd assignment with an even assignment.
Find the maximum root depth d; exactly half of the 2^d assignments have odd total, so return 2^(d-1).
Breadth-first search from node one to compute depths, take the maximum, and modularly exponentiate two to d-1.
The parity-flipping bijection proves the count is 2^(d-1), independent of which deepest node is selected.
editorial: The parity-flipping bijection proves the count is 2^(d-1), independent of which deepest node is selected.

tests.explanation: Only weight one makes the one-edge path sum odd, giving one assignment.
A deepest path has two edges; (1,2) and (2,1) are the two odd-sum assignments.
